problem_statement: cullenwebber/three-skull is a Vite-powered Codrops interactive-canvas demo: a full-bleed three.js/WebGPU (WebGL2 fallback) scene reveals a skull and figure through a fluid-simulation post-process, behind a fixed monospace 'frame' overlay. The frame chrome is a bare demo shell: a masthead heading 'Skeleton Fluid Reveal', Codrops metadata/author, a Tutorial link, an All demos link, a GitHub link, and #three.js / #webgpu tags -- no product voice or persona. Restyle the foreground stage-system chrome into a coherent fictional persona while preserving the running three.js skull scene untouched. Rebrand the masthead into 'Ossario Atelier', an anatomical vanitas studio staging cast-bone fluid reveals; add a short studio intro line; and build a compact on-scene 'Ossario Stage System' HUD control panel that extends the monochrome monospace frame. The panel carries a kicker, a 'Reliquary reveal chrome' heading, an intro, an interactive stage-focus selector (All layers / Cast / Veil / Room) with a live readout ('Now staging: X - N layers in view'), and the studio's labelled stage taxonomy as rows -- Cast (skull / figure relics), Veil (fluid vanitas wash), and Room (responsive dark frame). Clicking a focus button must recompute the readout and highlight the matching stage row. Shift the chrome accent palette (bone / oxblood) coherently. Keep the full-screen canvas, the fluid reveal, and the original Tutorial / All demos / GitHub / #three.js / #webgpu links intact and reachable on desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile.
required_content: The masthead heading reads 'Ossario Atelier' (an anatomical vanitas studio staging cast-bone fluid reveals) instead of 'Skeleton Fluid Reveal'.
A short studio intro line describes the persona ('anatomical vanitas studio staging cast-bone fluid reveals') beneath the masthead.

A compact on-scene Ossario Stage System HUD panel is present, headed by an 'Ossario Stage System' kicker and a 'Reliquary reveal chrome' heading, describing how the bone cast, fluid veil, and dark room compose as one vanitas study.

The HUD panel exposes an interactive stage-focus selector (All layers / Cast / Veil / Room) with a live readout that reads 'Now staging: All layers - 3 layers in view' initially and recomputes when a focus is chosen.
The HUD panel exposes the studio's stage taxonomy as labelled rows -- Cast (skull / figure relics), Veil (fluid vanitas wash), and Room (responsive dark frame) -- instead of raw Codrops demo labels.
Clicking the 'Cast' focus button recomputes the readout to 'Now staging: Cast - 1 layer in view' and highlights the Cast stage row.

The chrome adopts a coherent Ossario accent palette (bone / oxblood) across the kicker, intro, tags, selector, and panel borders while keeping the black-background monospace visual system and staying legible.
The full-screen three.js skull/fluid scene is preserved and still renders behind the chrome, and the original Tutorial, All demos, GitHub, #three.js, and #webgpu links remain visible and reachable.
No horizontal overflow at 390px mobile; the restyled chrome and HUD selector stay readable and correctly stacked across desktop, tablet, and mobile.

The stage-focus buttons carry class `stage-system__focus-btn` with `data-stage="all|cast|veil|room"` (the Cast button is `.stage-system__focus-btn[data-stage="cast"]`), and the live readout element carries class `stage-system__readout`, so the focus selector and readout are reachable by those hooks.
design_constraints: Preserve the three.js scene: do not remove, replace, or restyle the WebGPU/WebGL2 renderer, the fluid-simulation post-process, the GLB reveal assets, or the scene/postprocessing source.

The restyle is a foreground CHROME edit only (index.html + src/style.css + a small stage-system script): masthead heading, studio intro copy, Ossario Stage System HUD panel + stage-focus selector, accent palette; do not touch scene code, dependencies, or package scripts.
Preserve the demo's visual language: black background, white monospace typography, fixed frame overlay, thin borders, uppercase labels, compact link spacing, and full-bleed canvas behind the UI.

The stage-focus selector must actually recompute the live readout from the current selection (not a frozen snapshot), and the HUD panel must lay out without collapsing/overlapping and stay legible (no dark-on-dark).
Rebrand coherently around one persona (Ossario Atelier vanitas studio); do not leave a mix of the new wordmark and leftover Codrops / Skeleton Fluid Reveal labels.
The frame overlay keeps pointer-events: none (links + HUD controls stay pointer-events: auto) so the chrome never blocks the original links or canvas interaction.
Do not add stock imagery, remote fonts, CDN scripts, analytics, new routes, or explanatory how-to text outside the frame section; the chrome stays self-contained and console/network clean.

Wire the stage-focus selector with the exact hooks the HUD contract requires: each focus button uses class `stage-system__focus-btn` and a `data-stage` attribute (`all`, `cast`, `veil`, `room`); the labelled taxonomy rows live in a `stage-system__rows` container; the live readout uses class `stage-system__readout`. Clicking `.stage-system__focus-btn[data-stage="cast"]` must recompute the readout to `Now staging: Cast - 1 layer in view`.
state_constraints: desktop_home / mobile_home / tablet_home capture the running skull scene with the frame chrome + Ossario Stage System HUD across viewports; the demo baseline shows 'Skeleton Fluid Reveal', the Codrops author metadata, and no persona stage taxonomy.
desktop_canvas_click clicks the center of the canvas to confirm the frame overlay and HUD panel do not block interaction with the scene.

desktop_stage_focus clicks the HUD's 'Cast' stage-focus button and expects the live readout to recompute to 'Now staging: Cast - 1 layer in view' (changed from the 'All layers - 3 layers in view' pre-click state).
desktop_github_hover hovers the original GitHub link to confirm the preserved Codrops navigation links remain reachable after the restyle.
Source inspection confirms a Vite three.js/WebGPU demo whose GLB reveal assets are Draco-compressed and whose foreground frame chrome is a bare Codrops demo shell duplicated in index.html.

change_completion: The masthead, intro line, and Ossario Stage System HUD panel all read as the Ossario Atelier vanitas studio across the captured states.
The raw 'Skeleton Fluid Reveal' / Codrops demo labels no longer appear in the chrome, and the stage taxonomy (Cast / Veil / Room) frames the scene as a coherent vanitas study.
design_consistency: The restyle keeps the black-background monospace frame system, thin borders, uppercase labels, and compact spacing while adding a coherent, legible bone/oxblood accent.
The HUD panel and stage-focus selector lay out cleanly without collapsing, overlapping, or dark-on-dark illegibility, and read as one persona (Ossario Atelier).
regression: The full-screen three.js skull/fluid scene still renders behind the chrome (canvas screenshot bytes present).
The original Tutorial, All demos, GitHub, #three.js, and #webgpu links remain present and reachable, and canvas interaction is not blocked.
responsive: 390px mobile has no horizontal overflow and the chrome + HUD stage-focus selector stack cleanly.
The masthead, intro line, and HUD panel stay readable across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Vite three.js interactive-canvas restyle/cross_page task. The full-screen skull/fluid scene is preserved (regression); the restyle rebrands the foreground frame chrome into the Ossario Atelier vanitas studio and adds the on-scene 'Ossario Stage System' HUD control panel (masthead + intro + interactive All layers/Cast/Veil/Room stage-focus selector + live readout + Cast/Veil/Room stage taxonomy rows + bone/oxblood accent). The full-bleed canvas is position:fixed so it contributes 0 to documentElement.scrollWidth -- the HUD is the sole normal-flow chrome and carries every gate. baseline = the untouched Codrops demo layout (bare 'Skeleton Fluid Reveal' masthead, broken dark-on-dark HUD, no stage taxonomy) -> fails no_horizontal_overflow (fixed nowrap selector overflows 390px mobile), visual_regression (collapsed dark-on-dark HUD region vs the legible reference panel), and dom_assertions (the Cast/Veil/Room stage taxonomy is absent), but PASSES interaction_assertions (its readout wiring is correct). bad = a smart-wrong shallow HUD: the Ossario wordmark + focus selector + readout render and the click FIRES (buttons toggle .is-active), so it passes regression, but the stage taxonomy rows are never built (dom_assertions fail), the HUD region collapses into an overflowing dark-on-dark illegible toolbar (no_horizontal_overflow + visual_regression fail), and the readout is a frozen snapshot that never updates on click (interaction_assertions fail). All legs render the scene under swiftshader and are console/network clean (only benign WebGPU->WebGL2 + GL driver warnings; Draco decoder + favicon vendored locally). Image/SVG assets: the demo ships Draco-compressed .glb reveal models and a local favicon.svg; no stock imagery is added. This is a responsive, mobile-checked restyle.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: cullenwebber three-skull is a runnable Vite three.js/WebGPU fluid skull-reveal demo with a bare Codrops frame chrome over a full-bleed canvas, making it an ideal host for an experience-continuity restyle that rebrands the foreground chrome into the Ossario Atelier vanitas studio and adds an interactive on-scene stage-system HUD while preserving the running three.js scene.
